tasks.task: Review a codebase for the gaps behind most break-ins

items.when: Before reading line by line, to list every place outside data enters and how far each is trusted
When the client owns the code and wants access, sign-in and injection gaps ranked with fixes
When you want static tools to back up the manual read and leave rules the team can reuse
When the app is Django and the main question is who can see or change what
Before the report goes out, to catch findings stated without proof or a failed check left out

tasks.task: Review a pull request or diff for security risks

items.when: When a small change is pasted and a quick ranked list with the line and a fix is enough
When a pull request touches sign-in, access or data handling and needs a full security read
When the change needs the code around it read too, in order of what attackers use most
When the client wants the review comments fixed in code and a one-page sign-off as well

tasks.task: Fix API access, sign-in and input gaps with tests

items.when: Before any fix, to check each route's sign-in, access rule and input and list the gaps
When the gaps are known and each needs a fix, a test and a pull request a reviewer can follow
When you need test cases for wrong-user, no-token and bad-input calls on every route
When the fix has no tests around it and you must prove it holds and nothing else broke

tasks.task: Roll out security headers and a CSP without breaking the site

items.when: Before and after the change, to see which headers, HTTPS settings and content rules are missing
When you write the headers and a content policy that starts in report-only mode with a rollback

tasks.task: Harden sign-in, sessions and password storage

items.when: When roles and permissions were never written down and you need the plan before the code
When the job includes single sign-on, account recovery or session rules across several apps
When you write cookie and session settings or move password hashing without locking users out
When sign-in goes through another service and the right OAuth flow must be set up
When staff and customer sign-in needs a scored check and a password and second-step policy

tasks.task: Add input validation, output escaping and safe uploads

items.when: Before writing checks, to find every entry point and which ones have no filter yet
When you write the validation, escaping and upload rules for the client's routes
When one unsafe pattern keeps coming back and you want a tested rule that finds it everywhere
When each new check needs a test that sends bad input and proves it is refused

tasks.task: Add rate limits and bot protection to routes

items.when: Before blocking anything, to decide which bots and AI agents to allow, check or block
When routes have no limits and you need the right window for sign-in, search and write calls
When a shop sees fake orders or card testing and needs fraud rules and a review routine

tasks.task: Rank scanner and dependency findings into a patch order

items.when: When the client has no scan output yet and you need known weak packages and a parts list
When scan output is in and you need a ranked patch plan with exploited flaws first
When the fix means a major version jump that could break the build
Before upgrading, to see which behaviour has no test and could break without anyone noticing

tasks.task: Explain a scanner finding or CVE in plain words

items.when: When an alert names a weakness and someone must know if it matters for this app
When the owner asks what data could leak if the flaw were used
When a finding sounds frightening, to weigh the real risk against the cost of the fix

tasks.task: Respond to a leaked key, token or password

items.when: When a secret turns up in code, history, logs or chat and must be revoked in the right order
When one leak suggests more and the whole project needs a search, rotation and live check
After rotation, to check the live site no longer serves keys or private files to visitors
When new keys must be loaded and checked without the values showing in logs or chat
When the owner is alarmed, to separate what is known to be exposed from what is only feared

tasks.task: Check how keys and secrets are stored and rotated

items.when: When you need leaked keys found, env files tidied and a rotation plan for one project
When the team has no rule for where secrets live, who holds them and how often they change
When the code is on GitHub and pushes holding secrets should be blocked from now on
When the check finds a live secret and it must be handled at once

tasks.task: Add dependency, secret and code scans to CI

items.when: When a repository has no automatic security checks or a scan would have caught the last issue
When the team wants code scanning set up in their GitHub builds or on the command line
When secret scanning and push blocking must be switched on with a plan for each alert
When a flaw found in review should fail the build if anyone writes it again
When the build files are written, to find loose permissions and inputs an outsider controls

tasks.task: Threat model a new feature or app

items.when: At design stage or before a customer review, to write what can go wrong in about an hour
When the owner can only describe the system loosely and needs a first ranked list of attacks
When a larger system needs every part checked against six kinds of attack and rated by risk
When an API or config design makes the unsafe choice the easy one for developers
When a change lands on a system that has a threat model and the new risks must be recorded
When a control is proposed, to ask what it protects, what it costs and what it leaves open

tasks.task: Answer a customer's security questionnaire

items.when: When the questionnaire is long, to sort questions into must-haves and spot the ones you fail
When answers must be honest, backed by evidence and the same from one question to the next
When several people hold the facts and you need an evidence index and a list of open questions
Before sending, to catch any answer that claims a control with no proof behind it

tasks.task: Get ready for a customer security review or pen test

items.when: When a larger customer asks for a review, a test report or which standard the business follows
When the business follows no standard and needs a short first set of safeguards for its size
When the customer names SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA or PCI and you need a gap table against it
When the evidence is scattered and needs an index, a gap list and an owner for each item
When an outside tester will be hired and the scope and evidence rules must be set first

tasks.task: Scope and run an authorised scan of a running app

items.when: Before any scan or test of a running site, API or app, even a passive scan of staging
When the owner wants common web flaws checked on their own app and the fixes ranked
When written permission covers safe probing of a running app or API the client owns
When only a passive baseline is allowed: HTTPS, headers and files left open

tasks.task: Set up security.txt and a way to report flaws

items.when: When the business wants finders of a flaw to have a clear, safe way to report it
When a report arrives, to reproduce it and record what is verified before anyone replies
When a report looks serious and you need severity, who to tell and what to preserve

tasks.task: Run a launch security check on a small app

items.when: Before launch, to scope what is checked across code, servers, sign-in and daily running
When you want one pass for code flaws, weak packages and exposed secrets with a risk score
When the launch depends on a few routes that handle sign-in, payments or personal data
When the live site needs its HTTPS, headers and open files checked before launch day
When the owner needs a clear go or no-go with the blockers listed
When the plan assumes nobody will make a mistake, to ask what happens when someone does

tasks.task: Review AI-written code for security gaps

items.when: When an app was built fast with AI and may hold leaked keys or open database rules
When you want only the few risks that will hurt later, each with the smallest fix
When open Supabase rules are the gap and the app must reconnect with scoped access
When the team keeps coding with AI and wants a warning each time risky code is written

tasks.task: Check an AI feature, agent or MCP server for attack paths

items.when: Before an agent goes live, to rank risks in its tool access, plugins and behaviour
When an AI app must be tested for hidden instructions, jailbreaks and tool misuse
When the weak spots are known and layered defences must be added to the app
When a customer asks for findings against the published list of agent risks, with evidence
When the client runs an MCP server and needs its attack risks ranked with fixes
When an AI agent runs inside the build and outside text such as issue titles could reach it

tasks.task: Review cloud and infrastructure config for security gaps

items.when: When the set-up is in code files and you need open buckets and loose access rules ranked
When the client is on AWS and wants account-wide gaps ranked with fixes
When access policies grant too much and need tighter versions written

tasks.task: Run the monthly vulnerability and secrets sweep

items.when: Monthly, or at once when a widely reported flaw hits a package the client uses
When the client wants a weekly run that shows what is new, open or fixed since last time
During each sweep, to look again for keys in code and env files
When the sweep turns up new findings that need a place in the patch order

tasks.task: Triage a security alert or suspected break-in

items.when: When an alert comes in and you need severity, who to tell, what to keep and next steps
When you must work out which personal or payment data the attacker could have reached
When it is over and the client needs a blameless report with causes and follow-up owners
When customers must be told, to state plainly what was exposed and what they should do

tasks.task: Check how the app collects, keeps and deletes personal data

items.when: When nobody knows where personal data lives and deletion must reach every copy
When the code must support access, deletion and consent requests and you need the gaps
When a new feature uses personal data and a customer or regulator expects an assessment

always.when: Whenever keys or env files are in reach, so no secret value is printed, logged or repeated
Before any report or answer is sent, to confirm every claim has evidence you can point to

helpers.when: When a fix means reworking endpoints, webhooks or payment code, not just adding a check
When the job needs pipeline, container or cloud changes beyond the security checks
When the gaps are in staff accounts, devices, email or backups and not in the code
When the customer wants a full SOC 2, ISO 27001 or privacy programme, not one review
When fixes need a wider regression test run before release
When an AI feature must be rebuilt to resist hijacked instructions, not only tested

gaps: No library item writes security headers or a Content Security Policy, or reads CSP violation reports; only the kit covers it
No library item covers password hashing choice and migration, secure cookie settings, or JWT and session token handling
No library item covers safe file uploads: type checks, size limits, storage outside the web root and malware scanning
No library item writes output escaping or cross-site scripting and request forgery fixes for a named framework
No library item ranks CVEs by known exploitation and reachability; only the kit's triage skill does
No library item writes a vulnerability disclosure policy or handles an outside researcher's report through to a reply
No library item plans or reads an authorised dynamic scan such as an OWASP ZAP baseline; live testing items are general
No library item checks row-level database rules for Supabase or Firebase directly
No library item covers breach notification duties and deadlines by region for a small business
No library item reviews mobile app security: stored secrets, certificate checks and deep links
No library item reviews Dockerfile and container image security, or Kubernetes settings
No library item adds security logging and alerting so a break-in attempt is noticed
